title: Life-cycle rules, versioning, soft delete and immutability

videos.script: Lesson 2 ended with a log overwritten by one command, and nothing could bring it back. This lesson is about three ways to stop that. {{undo}} The first is soft delete. A deleted blob is kept for a number of days, and one request brings it back. {{soft}} The second is versioning. Every write keeps the content it replaced, so an overwrite loses nothing. {{versions}} Keeping everything has a price, so a life-cycle rule moves old blobs to cheaper tiers, and deletes what nobody needs. You declare one for Quitanda's exports. {{rule}} The third refuses the mistake instead of repairing it. An immutable blob cannot be overwritten or deleted, by anybody, until its date. {{lock}} Azurite accepts the soft delete setting, and then keeps nothing. You will watch that, and see it refuse the rest. {{weaker}} By the end you can say which protection each of Quitanda's containers needs, and what the lab can and cannot prove about it. {{end}}
